title: TypeScript: interfaces
summary: Describe the shape of an object with an interface and a union type.

quiz.q: What is an interface used for?
options: To run code when an object is created
To describe the shape (property names and types) of an object
To store data in the browser
quiz.explain: An interface only describes a shape. It disappears when the code is compiled, so it adds nothing to the running app.

quiz.template: interface Student { name: string; email___ string; }
quiz.explain: A question mark before the colon (`email?: string`) means the property may be missing.

quiz.q: Click the line TypeScript will reject.
quiz.explain: `b` is missing the required property `name`, so it does not match the `Student` shape.

options: Only the text 'A' or the text 'B'
quiz.explain: The `|` symbol builds a **union**: a value of type `Grade` must be exactly one of the listed options.

exercise.task:
Complete `student.ts`.

- Create an `interface Student` with `id: number`, `name: string` and an optional `email` of type `string`.
- Create a type `Grade` that is the union of `'A'`, `'B'` and `'C'`.
- Give the existing `topper` constant the type `Student`.
- Write a function `describe` that takes `s: Student`, returns a `string`, and builds the text from `s.id` and `s.name`.
hints: An interface looks like an object with types instead of values: `interface Student { ... }`.
Optional means `email?: string`. A union uses `|` between quoted texts. Annotate `topper` as `const topper: Student = ...`.
